findings.title: Error-based SQL injection in parameter 'id'
findings.detectionMethod: Active error-based: baseline vs. injected-probe signature diff
findings.preconditions: The tester is authorised to assess the target and the request reaches a code path that builds a SQL query.
findings.evidenceSummary:
Injecting a single quote produced a SQLite tokenizer error absent from the baseline.
Triggering probes: ['\'', "')"]
Signatures observed:
  • [SQLite] SQLITE_ERROR: unrecognized token
findings.limitations: Confidence reflects corroboration across probes. Manual verification recommended before escalation.
findings.remediation: Use parameterised queries / prepared statements for all database access. Never build SQL by concatenating untrusted input. Apply strict input validation (allow-lists) and least-privilege database accounts, and return generic error messages so database errors are not exposed to clients.
reproductionSteps: Send baseline request GET /rest/products/search?q=apple and note no SQL error.
Resend with q=apple' and observe the SQLite error in the response.
references: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet - https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html

evidence.testResponse:
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: text/html

SQLITE_ERROR: unrecognized token: "***REDACTED***"

findings.evidenceSummary:

  similarity(TRUE, baseline)=0.991  similarity(FALSE, baseline)=0.431
findings.limitations: Differential inference only; no data extracted.
